entry_state.expectation: A dusk elf with a specific agenda — every new contact in Barovia has one; the question is whether this agenda aligns with the party's
entry_state.fear: That Kasimir's resurrection plan will produce something worse than what he started with — that his grief will make him dangerous

exit_state.shift: Kasimir knows the path to the Amber Temple and is willing to guide them; whatever his motives, the alliance is practically valuable — and the party has learned to take practical value where they find it in Barovia

entry_state.expectation: A temple means structure, purpose, knowledge — ancient and dangerous, but knowable
entry_state.fear: That the Temple is not ancient and dormant but ancient and awake; that walking in was the first mistake

exit_state.shift: The Temple is nothing like a place of worship in any tradition the party recognizes — it is a prison, and the prisoners are interested in them

entry_state.expectation: The power is real, the cost is real — the question is whether the cost becomes real immediately or later, and the vestige is very comfortable with later
entry_state.fear: That accepting means becoming something they will not recognize; that refusing means failing when the power would have saved someone

exit_state.shift: Whether accepted or refused, the encounter with the vestige has changed something — the party member who stood at that sarcophagus now knows exactly what they are willing to trade, and that knowledge is not comfortable

entry_state.expectation: Getting out — the Temple has given them what it will give and taken what it will take; staying longer helps nothing
entry_state.fear: That Kasimir's confrontation with Patrina's vestige will produce something they cannot contain; that leaving will be harder than entering was

exit_state.shift: The party is out, which is what matters. What they carry out — in their hands and in their character sheets and in the changes written on whoever accepted a gift — is the permanent record of what the Temple cost them

entry_state.expectation: The party visits the Vistani camp outside Vallaki expecting the same hospitality as Tser Pool, or to follow up on Van Richten's mention of Arabelle
entry_state.fear: That whatever has happened to Arabelle connects to forces larger than a missing child, and that helping will cost them something they cannot afford right now

exit_state.shift: A child is missing. The party may have more context than the Vistani about where she is, which makes their role here uncomfortably close to someone who has information and is deciding whether to share it

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to find Arabelle and bring her back to the camp; the complication they did not fully anticipate is what Van Richten's reasons were
entry_state.fear: That either Van Richten's motives are darker than presented, or that returning Arabelle to the Vistani camp puts her in more danger than leaving her with Van Richten

exit_state.shift: The party has resolved the immediate question of where Arabelle is, but opened a larger question about what she is — and what Barovia has planned for her

entry_state.expectation: Ruins — another abandoned structure in a land full of them — but this one is large, and large ruins mean large dangers
entry_state.fear: That the dead knights within will not distinguish between the party and the enemies they have been standing vigil against for centuries

exit_state.shift: The revenants are not enemies and not allies — they are something in between, trapped in a purpose that has outlasted its context; the party understands they are walking through someone else's unfinished war

entry_state.expectation: A leader of the Order who will recognize the party as allies against Strahd and agree to light the beacon
entry_state.fear: That Vladimir's grief has made him unreasonable; that the one person who could activate the beacon will not

exit_state.shift: Vladimir is not wrong that Strahd deserves to suffer — but his method of ensuring that suffering has trapped his own knights as surely as Strahd's curse has trapped Barovia; the party must decide whether to work with him, around him, or in spite of him

entry_state.expectation: The skull is a trophy — Strahd keeps it displayed somewhere prominent; finding it means navigating the castle with a specific object in mind
entry_state.fear: That the skull's location is guarded specifically, or that retrieving it will require a confrontation they are not yet equipped for

exit_state.shift: Taking the skull is a small act of defiance against Strahd's display of conquest — the party has reclaimed something he took, and they feel the weight of that symbolism even if they cannot name it

entry_state.expectation: The party places Argynvost's skull in the mausoleum (area Q16) — they know from Argynvostholt's lore what should happen, but knowing does not make the silence before it happens easier to bear
entry_state.fear: That centuries of accumulated grief cannot be undone by a single act, that Vladimir's curse is too set to release, that the beacon will not come

exit_state.shift: When the dragon's spirit rises and the tower blazes silver, the party sees for the first time in this campaign what hope looks like from the outside — not the private stubborn hope of individuals holding on, but a signal that the rest of Barovia can see. Vladimir collapses. His war is over. The silence that follows is the cleanest thing the party will experience in Barovia.

entry_state.expectation: The party expects the woods to be an ordinary wild forest — strange perhaps, but passable and reversible
entry_state.fear: That something about this place is deeply wrong and they may have stepped into a trap

exit_state.shift: The party carries the visceral understanding that they cannot go back — the world they knew is no longer accessible from here

entry_state.expectation: The party hopes to find information, safety, or at least an explanation for the strangeness they have walked through
entry_state.fear: That the people of this place cannot or will not help them, and that there is no ordinary way home

exit_state.shift: The party has seen oppression written into the faces of people who have forgotten what hope looks like — the danger is no longer abstract, it lives in every shuttered window and averted gaze

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to be observers in this village — strangers in a strange land, not yet responsible for anyone's fate
entry_state.fear: That responsibility for real people's suffering is about to be placed on their shoulders before they understand the rules of this world

exit_state.shift: Ireena's situation has made the danger personal and human — the party now carries the weight of knowing there is a specific person who will be harmed if they fail

entry_state.expectation: The party expected to operate unnoticed for a while longer — to gather information before the danger noticed them
entry_state.fear: That they are already known, already claimed, and that the game they have been thrust into has rules they do not understand

exit_state.shift: The party understands for the first time that Strahd views them as pieces on his board — the invitation is not hospitality, it is ownership, and refusing it changes nothing

entry_state.expectation: The party hopes that forward motion means progress — that moving away from the village moves them away from immediate danger
entry_state.fear: That the road will confirm there is no safe place in Barovia, only different kinds of danger

exit_state.shift: The party has accepted that they are not travelers passing through — they are participants in this world's suffering, and the only direction that makes sense is toward the thing that caused it

entry_state.expectation: The party expects the road to the castle to be the last test before the test that matters — difficult but navigable with what they now carry
entry_state.fear: That no preparation is ever truly enough, that the castle's looming presence is Strahd already winning before they arrive

exit_state.shift: The castle does not need to say anything — its presence alone communicates that Strahd has been waiting, that this is his arena, and that every step taken toward those gates is taken on his terms

entry_state.expectation: The party expects combat at the gate — to fight their way in, which is something they know how to do
entry_state.fear: That the open gates are not an oversight but an invitation, and that being let in is more dangerous than being kept out

exit_state.shift: Inside the castle, reality bends to Strahd's will — the party has entered a place where their skills matter less than his permission, and they feel the geometry of control closing around them

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to navigate and fight their way through to Strahd — a terrible but comprehensible gauntlet
entry_state.fear: That the castle is infinite, that Strahd can keep them trapped and attrited until nothing is left

exit_state.shift: Having survived the castle's malice — the shifting corridors, the impossible traps, the endless servants — the party arrives at Strahd carrying a grim clarity: they have passed every test except the last one

entry_state.expectation: The party expects everything they have done to be enough — that preparation, sacrifice, and will are the variables that determine this outcome
entry_state.fear: That Strahd is simply too powerful, that centuries of existence and mastery over his domain cannot be overcome no matter what they carry

exit_state.shift: The battle does not resolve into clarity — every party member carries the knowledge that they stood in that moment and were tested against something older and stranger than they are, and the outcome has changed them regardless of which direction it fell

entry_state.expectation: The party has committed everything to this moment — the expectation is survival, not triumph, as the battle reaches its climax
entry_state.fear: That Strahd will not fall, that even the Sunsword is not enough, that they will die here and the curse will deepen

exit_state.shift: When the sunlight breaks through for the first time in a century, the party does not feel triumph — they feel the ache of everything it cost and the profound quiet of a world that has exhaled a breath it has been holding for generations

entry_state.expectation: The party entered this battle believing their preparation had tipped the odds — that sacrifice plus artifacts plus allies equals a survivable fight
entry_state.fear: That the math was always wrong, that Strahd in his own domain cannot be reduced to a calculation

exit_state.shift: There is no after for the party — but for anyone who witnesses or survives adjacent to this ending, what remains is the particular grief of watching people who chose hope be consumed by the darkness they walked toward

entry_state.expectation: The party expects the battle to be decided by force — that Strahd can only be stopped, not reached
entry_state.fear: That mercy or love is not a tactical option in a fight for survival

exit_state.shift: Witnessing Strahd's redemption does not feel like victory — it feels like grief that came too late, and a tenderness for what love costs when it arrives after centuries of darkness; the party carries a question they cannot answer: was it worth it

entry_state.expectation: The party enters the church expecting a sanctuary — the one kind of place in Barovia where the darkness reliably cannot reach
entry_state.fear: That even the sacred spaces in Barovia are not what they should be

exit_state.shift: The sanctuary the party was counting on does not currently exist, and the window for restoring it is closing

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to find the bones guarded by servants of Strahd and to have to fight their way to them
entry_state.fear: That the coffin maker's shop is more heavily fortified than it appears, or that the bones have already been moved

exit_state.shift: The party retrieved the bones, but the cost was real — the coffin maker's shop was a nest, and clearing it was not clean work

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to return the bones and have the church's protection restored immediately
entry_state.fear: That they will arrive too late — that the festival has already begun, or that vampire spawn are already inside

exit_state.shift: The church is safe. They did the thing that needed doing, and it worked. In Barovia, this is enough to feel genuinely significant

entry_state.expectation: The party expects a guarded location and a fight — they have been told where to go and they are ready to take what must be taken
entry_state.fear: That the sacred place will judge them unworthy, that holiness in this cursed land might have its own test they cannot pass

exit_state.shift: Holding the holy symbol in a land where faith is a form of defiance gives the party something they have lacked — a tangible piece of resistance against Strahd's total dominion

entry_state.expectation: The party expects a powerful artifact in a guarded place — a worthy challenge with a worthy prize at the end
entry_state.fear: That the Sunsword's awakening will alert Strahd and bring consequences they are not yet ready to face

exit_state.shift: When the Sunsword ignites, the party feels both powerful and visible — they have declared themselves openly to Strahd, and the relief of holding the light does not erase the dread of what it has announced

entry_state.expectation: The party expects the Tome to be the most dangerous retrieval — Strahd's most personal possession, most heavily guarded
entry_state.fear: That reading Strahd's private history will reveal something that makes him harder to hate, or that the knowledge within will show them how unlikely their victory truly is

exit_state.shift: The Tome's contents are a wound — to know Strahd's history, his grief, and the nature of his corruption is to hold knowledge that complicates the simplicity of killing him, even as it equips them to do so

entry_state.expectation: The party expects this moment to feel triumphant — the culmination of weeks of sacrifice finally held in their hands
entry_state.fear: That the weight of what must come next will crush the satisfaction — that holding the tools of victory does not guarantee it

exit_state.shift: The party has run out of reasons to delay — holding all three artifacts, they face the truth that they have become the people this moment requires, or they have not, and there is only one way to find out

entry_state.expectation: The children seem genuinely afraid — helping them feels like a simple, human act of decency in an otherwise overwhelming land
entry_state.fear: That what awaits inside is far worse than the mist-shrouded street outside

exit_state.shift: The door has closed. The street is gone. The party understands they have stepped into something they cannot simply step back out of

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to find the children's parents, perhaps disturbed or mad, and to deal with whatever creature lurks below
entry_state.fear: That the full truth of this house will be more terrible than a simple monster

exit_state.shift: The party has discovered that the children were murdered by their own parents as cult offerings, and that they have been guided through this house by the ghosts of those children ever since

entry_state.expectation: The party expects the house to release them once they face whatever waits in the ritual chamber below
entry_state.fear: That the only exit requires them to become the very thing the cult was — people who sacrifice innocents to dark powers

exit_state.shift: The party is outside. They are alive. But something has shifted in how they understand survival in Barovia — it is not a clean thing, and the cost of it is visible on every face

entry_state.expectation: The party has prepared for this; they know what they want the festival to produce and have made their choices leading up to it
entry_state.fear: That the festival's outcome will be more chaotic than planned, regardless of which direction the chaos runs

exit_state.shift: Vallaki has changed — either the Baron's grip has tightened or it has broken — and the town that exists now is different from the one the party entered

entry_state.expectation: The party did not expect the arrest — or expected it and could not avoid it — and is now in a situation that their resources and planning did not account for
entry_state.fear: That they will be here long enough for the larger mission to be compromised, and that getting out will require burning bridges they cannot afford to burn

exit_state.shift: The party is out of the stockade by the end of this scene, one way or another, but how they got out will have shaped their remaining relationships in Vallaki

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to find Van Richten ready to be recruited — a legendary hunter who surely wants to finish what he started
entry_state.fear: That the man they find will be a shadow of the legend, or that he will refuse them and they will face Strahd alone

exit_state.shift: The search itself — the false leads, the evasive villagers, the weeks of uncertainty — has tested the party's commitment; finding Van Richten's trail means they have earned the right to knock on his door

entry_state.expectation: The party expects their arrival and the Tarokka's endorsement to be sufficient — that a legend will recognize other heroes
entry_state.fear: That Van Richten's suspicion will be a wall they cannot climb, and that the fated ally will turn them away

exit_state.shift: Van Richten's wariness has shown the party that past failures have costs that still compound — they realize they must prove themselves rather than simply claim their fated role

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to need to argue their case — to perform competence under a skeptic's gaze
entry_state.fear: That no argument will be enough, that Van Richten's grief and failure are a wall no evidence can breach

exit_state.shift: Van Richten's agreement is not enthusiasm — it is a tired man choosing to try once more — and the party feels the gravity of what they have asked him to risk, not just what they have gained

entry_state.expectation: The party expects Ezmerelda to be a bonus — another asset following Van Richten's lead
entry_state.fear: That she will see through them where Van Richten's hope made him generous

exit_state.shift: Ezmerelda's fearlessness is contagious — where Van Richten's decision was heavy with sacrifice, her joining feels like genuine belief that the party can win, and that belief is its own kind of armor

entry_state.expectation: The party expects a walled village to offer at least basic shelter and safety from the dangers of the Svalich Woods
entry_state.fear: That the gates will stay shut — that even in Barovia, hospitality has limits the party cannot overcome

exit_state.shift: The party has passed their first test of persuasion in Krezk; they know entry was earned, not given, and that the Burgomaster's trust is conditional

entry_state.expectation: The party expects a holy man in a holy place — sanctuary, guidance, perhaps healing
entry_state.fear: That the Abbey is another trap; that safety in Barovia is always a surface concealing something worse

exit_state.shift: The Abbot's power and certainty are undeniable, but his plan is monstrous — the party must decide what they believe about ends justifying means, and whether helping him is collaboration or strategy

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to see some evidence of The Abbot's project — the bride he mentioned — but imagines something abstract, unfinished
entry_state.fear: That the thing in the room will be recognizably human enough to make what The Abbot is doing undeniable

exit_state.shift: The horror is not that The Abbot is evil — he is not, or was not — but that something that started with the intention to help has produced this; the party must now decide what to do with that knowledge

entry_state.expectation: The party must answer the Abbot's proposal — he has been serene and helpful and genuinely pleased by their presence, and he is also building a flesh golem from the bodies of his mongrelfolk congregation as a gift for Strahd
entry_state.fear: That accepting legitimizes what he is doing; that refusing means losing the most powerful healer in Barovia at a point in the campaign where they will need exactly that

exit_state.shift: The Abbey visit ends. The party descends back to Krezk's quiet streets carrying whatever moral position they arrived at — acceptance, refusal, or the uncomfortable pragmatism of a deferred answer. The Abbot remains above them in his high place, still serene, still certain his plan will bring peace.

entry_state.expectation: An old woman selling food on the road is unusual but not inherently threatening — the party is tired and the smell of the pastries is genuinely wonderful
entry_state.fear: That the smell is too wonderful; that nothing in Barovia smells this good without a reason

exit_state.shift: The encounter has left the party with an unresolved question — the pies were real and the woman seemed harmless, but the windmill behind her has a particular quality that does not resolve into comfort on reflection

entry_state.expectation: The party expects a problem they can fight or flee from; this is a problem they cannot do either with
entry_state.fear: That the affected person will not wake up; that the dream is consuming them from inside

exit_state.shift: The horror of watching someone disappear into a dream has clarified what must be done — Morgantha must be confronted, and the party is no longer uncertain about whether the fight is justified

entry_state.expectation: A fight, or at least a direct confrontation — the party is done with subtlety
entry_state.fear: That Morgantha is more powerful than them, that the children are being used as leverage, and that winning here will cost more than they can afford

exit_state.shift: The confrontation is over, but the windmill has left a residue — whatever the outcome, the party has seen what Barovia does to the innocent when no one intervenes, and they carry that forward

entry_state.expectation: Ruins mean abandoned; abandoned means empty; empty means manageable
entry_state.fear: That the ruins are not abandoned; that the stillness of the floodwater is the stillness of something waiting

exit_state.shift: The party has crossed into the ruins and the feeling of being watched has not diminished — it has become a certainty; they are in someone's domain, and that someone knows it

entry_state.expectation: A hard fight against something ancient and malevolent; victory possible but not guaranteed
entry_state.fear: That Baba Lysaga is not just powerful but genuinely beyond what they can manage — that Barovia has handed them an enemy they cannot defeat

exit_state.shift: Baba Lysaga is not a villain with a plan; she is grief calcified into mania over centuries, and beating her feels less like triumph than like surviving a natural disaster

entry_state.expectation: The party seeks guidance — they expect a fortune teller, mysterious but ultimately human, who might offer clues they can act on
entry_state.fear: That what they learn will be too vague to use, or will confirm that their situation is hopeless

exit_state.shift: Madam Eva's recognition of them — her sense that she has been waiting — removes the party's last illusion that their arrival was accidental; they feel the weight of something larger having moved to put them here

entry_state.expectation: The party hopes the cards will give them something actionable — a map, a name, a plan
entry_state.fear: That what the cards reveal will demand more than they are capable of giving

exit_state.shift: The reading has handed them a mission that is both entirely clear and enormously daunting — they now know exactly what must be done and exactly how far they are from being able to do it

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to debate the reading and perhaps find a reason to question it — to retain some sense that their choices are their own
entry_state.fear: That accepting the reading means accepting they are not free agents but instruments of a fate already written

exit_state.shift: The party has stopped resisting the weight of the mission and chosen to carry it — the shift from refugee to quester is internal, not external, and this is the moment it happens

entry_state.expectation: A walled town suggests safety, order, and resources — the party has been in the dark long enough to want all three
entry_state.fear: That the walls are keeping something in as much as keeping something out

exit_state.shift: The town is walled and populated, which is better than the woods, but the mandatory cheer is a different kind of wrong — not supernatural, but deeply human, and perhaps more difficult to navigate

entry_state.expectation: The party hopes the Baron is a reasonable leader who might offer resources and cooperation against Strahd
entry_state.fear: That the mandatory festival notices were not exaggeration and the person running this town is genuinely dangerous in a petty, unpredictable way

exit_state.shift: The Baron is sincere, which makes him more dangerous than a cynical tyrant — a man who genuinely believes what he is doing is right cannot be argued out of it, only outmaneuvered

entry_state.expectation: The party expects the festival preparation to be perfunctory compliance with an annoying local custom
entry_state.fear: That genuine compliance means becoming part of the system, while resistance means becoming a target before they are ready

exit_state.shift: The party has taken a position — visible compliance or quiet resistance — and the town has begun to form an opinion of them accordingly

entry_state.expectation: The party expects a political opponent to the Baron — probably more reasonable, possibly useful, likely self-interested
entry_state.fear: That every powerful figure in Vallaki has an agenda that serves their own survival rather than anyone else's

exit_state.shift: Lady Wachter is clearly the more rational of the two faction leaders, which makes her devil-worship feel more deliberate and therefore more dangerous than the Baron's sincere delusion

entry_state.expectation: The party must weigh two imperfect options — a delusional tyrant and a capable devil-worshipper — and decide which Vallaki serves their larger purpose better
entry_state.fear: That either choice installs a leader who will, in a different way, harm the people they have been trying to protect

exit_state.shift: The choice has been made. In Barovia, choices without good options are the standard, and the party is learning to make them without paralysis

entry_state.expectation: The party knows they cannot be in Vallaki long without choosing a side — staying neutral is itself a position, and both factions will test it before long
entry_state.fear: That the choice they make here will harden into consequences they cannot undo; that backing either faction means absorbing that faction's costs

exit_state.shift: The decision is made. The party knows whose house they will sleep in, whose guards will not stop them at the gates, and whose enemies they have quietly made. Vallaki is still a town under Strahd's shadow, but it is now a town they have a position in — however uncomfortable that position may be.

entry_state.expectation: The Blue Water Inn is where travelers and locals mix, and the party hopes to gather information in a less formal context than official meetings
entry_state.fear: That everyone in Vallaki is being watched, including at the inn, and that open conversation is a liability

exit_state.shift: Rictavio is clearly not who he says he is, and the question of who he actually is feels more important than any of the inn's other gossip

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to confront the disguised figure and confirm their suspicion that he is something more than a carnival master
entry_state.fear: That he will deny everything, or that he will confirm who he is and immediately refuse to help

exit_state.shift: Van Richten is everything his reputation promised — knowledgeable, capable, and deeply damaged by the cost of what he knows — and his reluctance to engage is not cowardice but a calculation based on consequences the party cannot yet fully appreciate

entry_state.expectation: The party knows who Van Richten is — now they need what he knows. He will share it, but on his terms, with the economy of a man who has learned not to waste effort on people who will not survive the week
entry_state.fear: That he knows too much — that his intelligence will make the scale of the threat more legible and therefore more terrifying; that the party will leave this conversation less confident than they arrived

exit_state.shift: The briefing ends. The party now understands the structure of what they are up against: the Tarokka reading, the three items, the Dark Powers, the anchoring mechanism. It is not comforting information. It is precise information, which is a different kind of useful. Van Richten tells them where he will be if they need him — his tower, north of the lake — and makes no promises beyond availability.

entry_state.expectation: The party hopes the village priest might offer them guidance, shelter, or information about the land they have entered
entry_state.fear: That the people of this village are so broken by what they live under that no useful help can be found here

exit_state.shift: The party has seen what hope looks like when it has been hollowed out — Donavich is a man of faith who has lost his faith's ability to protect anyone he loves

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to find something monstrous below; they are less prepared for something that also seems like a person
entry_state.fear: That the right thing to do and the kind thing to do are not the same thing

exit_state.shift: The party has made a decision that cannot be unmade, for someone else's son, in front of that someone else — and they will carry the weight of whatever they chose

entry_state.expectation: The party returns from the church basement carrying the decision they made about Doru — whether they destroyed him or simply walked away, the outcome of that choice is now Father Donavich's to absorb
entry_state.fear: That there was no right answer, and the wrong one will haunt them; that Father Donavich's grief is too broken to be helped by anything they can do

exit_state.shift: The church is quieter when they leave it. Whether Donavich weeps or prays or simply stares at the floor, something has ended here — the party steps back into the fog of Barovia's roads knowing they have just made the first irreversible decision of the campaign

entry_state.expectation: The party hopes the Vistani camp will offer food, rest, and perhaps information — things that have been scarce since entering Barovia
entry_state.fear: That the Vistani's famous freedom of movement through Barovia comes at a cost the party does not yet understand

exit_state.shift: The warmth of the camp and the quality of the welcome have lowered the party's guard — which is exactly what was intended, and which may be exactly right

entry_state.expectation: A straightforward crossing — the lake is still and the tower is visible on the far side
entry_state.fear: That nothing in Barovia is ever as straightforward as it looks; that the dark water hides something

exit_state.shift: The crossing has passed without catastrophe, but the silence of the lake has left something behind — a sense of being observed from below, or from the grey sky, or from nowhere in particular

entry_state.expectation: A den means a contained space, confined opponents, the possibility of stealth — if the approach is managed well, the children can be freed before Kiril knows the party is there
entry_state.fear: That the den is not as contained as it looks; that the pack has numbers and the party does not; that silver weapons will not be enough

exit_state.shift: The den is resolved, but werewolves in Barovia are not simply monsters — they are people who were cursed, and the party has had to make decisions about that distinction under pressure

entry_state.expectation: The children are in wooden cages in the shrine — the party knows where they are and must get them out before Kiril's return triggers the Die Kinder event, in which he hunts the children himself if they flee while he lives
entry_state.fear: That Kiril returns before the children are safely away; that the traumatized children will not cooperate with calm; that the party cannot fight the full pack and carry children at the same time

exit_state.shift: The children are out. They are not okay — they have been in cages in a cave full of werewolves — but they are breathing, and they are moving, and the wereraven observer from Krezk is already there to guide them west toward the village. The pack behind the party is either silent because Kiril is dead, or temporarily leaderless. Either way, the mountain cave recedes. The road down feels longer than the road up.

entry_state.expectation: A winery problem — druids and plant creatures — sounds concrete and solvable compared to the supernatural weight of Strahd
entry_state.fear: That even a solvable problem in Barovia is more complicated than it appears, and that the Martikovs are not telling them everything

exit_state.shift: The party has accepted an obligation to people who need them — in Barovia, that is rare enough to matter

entry_state.expectation: The ritual is already underway — the party is working against a clock, not just against opponents
entry_state.fear: That they are too late; that the gem will be consumed by the ritual before they can interrupt it

exit_state.shift: The hill has been cleared or the ritual completed, and either way Yester Hill has left marks — on the party's resources, on the land, and on their understanding of how Strahd's influence operates through proxies who do not even know they are serving him

entry_state.expectation: A task completed; the winery clear; the Martikovs able to come home
entry_state.fear: That the victory feels too small — that clearing a winery and returning wine production to a doomed land is an insufficient use of whatever time they have

exit_state.shift: The winery restoration is proof that things in Barovia can be fixed — small things, practical things; the party needed that proof more than they knew

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to be the hunter in this moment — they have direction, they know what they are seeking
entry_state.fear: That Strahd is always a step ahead, that their plan is already known and already countered

exit_state.shift: Losing an artifact to Strahd does not simply set back the quest — it reveals that Strahd has been watching, toying, and waiting, and that the party's sense of control was always an illusion he permitted

entry_state.expectation: A toymaker's shop in a grim town — probably just grim toys
entry_state.fear: That something about this place will make Ireena's situation more precarious than it already is

exit_state.shift: The dolls make Strahd's obsession with Ireena feel personal and immediate in a way that abstract warnings did not — he has been watching her, perhaps for years

entry_state.expectation: The party knows who Van Richten is — now they need what he knows. He will share it, but on his terms, with the economy of a man who has learned not to waste effort on people who will not survive the week
entry_state.fear: That he knows too much — that his intelligence will make the scale of the threat more legible and therefore more terrifying; that the party will leave this conversation less confident than they arrived

exit_state.shift: The briefing ends. The party now understands the structure of what they are up against: the Tarokka reading, the three items, the Dark Powers, the anchoring mechanism. It is not comforting information. It is precise information, which is a different kind of useful. Van Richten tells them where he will be if they need him — his tower, north of the lake — and makes no promises beyond availability.

entry_state.expectation: The party expects their sincerity or preparation to be visible enough to break through Van Richten's hesitation
entry_state.fear: That they have already shown some flaw — overconfidence, lack of evidence, or disrespect — that has already closed the door

exit_state.shift: The refusal confronts the party with the gap between who they believe themselves to be and who Van Richten sees — they must reckon with what they failed to demonstrate

latest_exit_state.shift: The refusal confronts the party with the gap between who they believe themselves to be and who Van Richten sees — they must reckon with what they failed to demonstrate

entry_state.expectation: The party expected to operate unnoticed for a while longer — to gather information before the danger noticed them
entry_state.fear: That they are already known, already claimed, and that the game they have been thrust into has rules they do not understand

exit_state.shift: The party understands for the first time that Strahd views them as pieces on his board — the invitation is not hospitality, it is ownership, and refusing it changes nothing

entry_state.expectation: The party expects everything they have done to be enough — that preparation, sacrifice, and will are the variables that determine this outcome
entry_state.fear: That Strahd is simply too powerful, that centuries of existence and mastery over his domain cannot be overcome no matter what they carry

exit_state.shift: The battle does not resolve into clarity — every party member carries the knowledge that they stood in that moment and were tested against something older and stranger than they are, and the outcome has changed them regardless of which direction it fell

entry_state.expectation: The party has committed everything to this moment — the expectation is survival, not triumph, as the battle reaches its climax
entry_state.fear: That Strahd will not fall, that even the Sunsword is not enough, that they will die here and the curse will deepen

exit_state.shift: When the sunlight breaks through for the first time in a century, the party does not feel triumph — they feel the ache of everything it cost and the profound quiet of a world that has exhaled a breath it has been holding for generations

entry_state.expectation: The party entered this battle believing their preparation had tipped the odds — that sacrifice plus artifacts plus allies equals a survivable fight
entry_state.fear: That the math was always wrong, that Strahd in his own domain cannot be reduced to a calculation

exit_state.shift: There is no after for the party — but for anyone who witnesses or survives adjacent to this ending, what remains is the particular grief of watching people who chose hope be consumed by the darkness they walked toward

entry_state.expectation: The party expects the battle to be decided by force — that Strahd can only be stopped, not reached
entry_state.fear: That mercy or love is not a tactical option in a fight for survival

exit_state.shift: Witnessing Strahd's redemption does not feel like victory — it feels like grief that came too late, and a tenderness for what love costs when it arrives after centuries of darkness; the party carries a question they cannot answer: was it worth it

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to be the hunter in this moment — they have direction, they know what they are seeking
entry_state.fear: That Strahd is always a step ahead, that their plan is already known and already countered

exit_state.shift: Losing an artifact to Strahd does not simply set back the quest — it reveals that Strahd has been watching, toying, and waiting, and that the party's sense of control was always an illusion he permitted

entry_state.expectation: The party believes their momentum and willingness to fight is enough — that courage can substitute for preparation
entry_state.fear: That hesitation is the only real enemy, that waiting any longer will cost more than going now

exit_state.shift: Being repelled by the castle is not just a tactical setback — it is Strahd teaching them that he controls the terms of this confrontation, and that they have shown him exactly what they lack

latest_exit_state.shift: Being repelled by the castle is not just a tactical setback — it is Strahd teaching them that he controls the terms of this confrontation, and that they have shown him exactly what they lack

entry_state.expectation: The party expects a holy man in a holy place — sanctuary, guidance, perhaps healing
entry_state.fear: That the Abbey is another trap; that safety in Barovia is always a surface concealing something worse

exit_state.shift: The Abbot's power and certainty are undeniable, but his plan is monstrous — the party must decide what they believe about ends justifying means, and whether helping him is collaboration or strategy

entry_state.expectation: The party expects to see some evidence of The Abbot's project — the bride he mentioned — but imagines something abstract, unfinished
entry_state.fear: That the thing in the room will be recognizably human enough to make what The Abbot is doing undeniable

exit_state.shift: The horror is not that The Abbot is evil — he is not, or was not — but that something that started with the intention to help has produced this; the party must now decide what to do with that knowledge

entry_state.expectation: The party must answer the Abbot's proposal — he has been serene and helpful and genuinely pleased by their presence, and he is also building a flesh golem from the bodies of his mongrelfolk congregation as a gift for Strahd
entry_state.fear: That accepting legitimizes what he is doing; that refusing means losing the most powerful healer in Barovia at a point in the campaign where they will need exactly that

exit_state.shift: The Abbey visit ends. The party descends back to Krezk's quiet streets carrying whatever moral position they arrived at — acceptance, refusal, or the uncomfortable pragmatism of a deferred answer. The Abbot remains above them in his high place, still serene, still certain his plan will bring peace.

entry_state.expectation: A leader of the Order who will recognize the party as allies against Strahd and agree to light the beacon
entry_state.fear: That Vladimir's grief has made him unreasonable; that the one person who could activate the beacon will not

exit_state.shift: Vladimir is not wrong that Strahd deserves to suffer — but his method of ensuring that suffering has trapped his own knights as surely as Strahd's curse has trapped Barovia; the party must decide whether to work with him, around him, or in spite of him

entry_state.expectation: The party places Argynvost's skull in the mausoleum (area Q16) — they know from Argynvostholt's lore what should happen, but knowing does not make the silence before it happens easier to bear
entry_state.fear: That centuries of accumulated grief cannot be undone by a single act, that Vladimir's curse is too set to release, that the beacon will not come

exit_state.shift: When the dragon's spirit rises and the tower blazes silver, the party sees for the first time in this campaign what hope looks like from the outside — not the private stubborn hope of individuals holding on, but a signal that the rest of Barovia can see. Vladimir collapses. His war is over. The silence that follows is the cleanest thing the party will experience in Barovia.
